# Review, pass 1 — iliad-075 (Iliad 12.277–377)

Method: every note label and cross-reference checked against the line; Greek to `l` word by word; `l` against `i`; house tables (Iliad and Odyssey conventions) grepped for every stock word; published roots read for 4.198, 4.285, 4.342, 5.91, 6.194–195, 8.161–162, 2.153; quotation marks and `mark` checked; all 101 lines run through the scanner. `t` untouched (checked: every `t` identical before and after). Edits made by script, 38 field edits in 18 units.

Counts: 0 high, 9 medium, 10 low (19 changes), plus 8 findings refused.

## Findings considered and refused

- **12.304 σταθμοῖο δίεσθαι.** Kept "be driven from the steading": it is the usual reading, matches ἀπείρητος "untried" and `i`; the alternative ("flee from") is not better supported. Note now says the sense is not certain (low change above).
- **12.322 περί + φυγόντε.** Kept `l` "about this war, we two having escaped" (literal) and `i` "once we had escaped this war"; the note already says the construction is unusual and states the sense. Nothing more can be said with certainty.
- **12.277 μάχην Ἀχαιῶν.** Kept the possessive genitive ("the fighting of the Achaeans"): ὀτρύνω takes a person in the accusative, so Ἀχαιῶν cannot be the object here; `i` "urged on the Achaeans’ fighting" agrees. Only the table word "fighting" for l changed.
- **12.287–289 βαλλομένων.** Note is right that it agrees with τῶν (the men, genitive absolute); `l` "the men being pelted" and `i` "as the men were pelted" both carry that. The unit boundary after βαλλομένων is a sense-unit break at the ano teleia and is fine. 338–339 is a different βαλλομένων, with σακέων.
- **τόξων ἐῢ εἰδώς, 350 and 363, "who knows the bow well".** Kept. The table's "who knew the bow well" is for narrative past (2.718, 4.196); here the participle stands in a present command and the English tense follows the sentence; the drafter recorded the departure in new-renderings.md. Both repetitions agree.
- **12.338 κτύπος "thud".** Kept: the table has κτύπος "thud" (10.532, 10.535) and δοῦπος "thud" (9.573); the note says both words get "thud" and why.
- **12.317 πύκα θωρηκτάων "closely corseleted".** Kept: literal, and the note says it is not known whether πύκα speaks of fit or strength.
- **κακότητα φέροντες "evil bringing" / "bringing misfortune".** Kept: l "evil" is the table's own for 10.70–71; i "misfortune" is the table's (23.238, 11.382). Also kept: κοιρανέουσιν "act as rulers" (a documented departure like 2.207, 4.230), the single-quote mark at 318, `i` "who could never have enough of war" at 335 (the table's tense for ἀκόρητος is present, but narrative past is natural here).

## Checks recorded

- **Citations.** 4.198 (iliad-023, ln 198) = line 351, herald again: true. 4.285 (iliad-024, ln 285), Agamemnon speaking, Αἴαντ’ vocative: true. 4.342 (iliad-024, ln 341–342), second line of the unit = 316: true. 5.91 (iliad-027, ln 89–91), half-line ὅτ’ ἐπιβρίσῃ Διὸς ὄμβρος, English kept: true. 6.195 (iliad-037, ln 194): true, English now matches. 8.162 (iliad-047, ln 161–162, Hector to Diomedes): true; the published line has δεπάεσσι and ours δεπάεσσιν (movable ν), English identical. Odyssey 6.134 = 12.301 (packet) and 6.130 half-line: true. 4.69 = 365's model: true. 7.386 added as the model for ἠνώγει.
- **Quotation marks.** Four speeches, “ and ” counts 4/4 in l and in i. Sarpedon 310–328 (one inner speech 318–321 in single ‘ ’, closed before he resumes at 322, so the outer speech needs no new mark), Menestheus 343–348, Thoötes 354–363, Ajax 366–369. Single ‘ ’ for a speech inside a speech is the house practice: iliad-044, unit at ln 299–302 (the gift-exchange speech): ‘ opens the quoted words, ’ closes them before the closing ”. (The only published precedent; it has no `mark` because it shares a unit with the speech's end. The 318 `mark` "What a Lycian will say" is kept: it is the first unit of a speech and helps the reader.) Neighbour: iliad-074's last unit (ln 275) closes the Ajaxes’ speech with ”, so nothing runs into this part. This part ends outside a speech.
- **Paragraph marks `p`.** At 277, 290, 329 (the unit begins the ¶-line), 351, 364, 370: match the packet.
- **Scansion.** Packet flags none. Scanner on all 101 lines: no unscannable line; "spondaic fifth" notes at 317, 347, 360 are regular spondeiazons, not irregularities; 288’s scanner licence is from reading the final -ας of Τρῶας (long) as short. No note added.
- **Accents/breathing.** εὕρῃσι has rough breathing, so χ’ for κε in 302 is correct.

# Review, pass 2 — iliad-075 (Iliad 12.277–377)

Method: every note label and cross-reference re-read against the line (all 47 units; the 12.xxx references to 278, 284, 287, 289, 315, 344–350, 356 and the published 4.198, 4.285, 4.342, 4.69, 5.91, 6.195, 8.162, 7.386, Odyssey 6.130–134 re-checked); `l` against `i` again; then `gloss.json` checked entry by entry against its line in `units.json` (110 novel entries and 27 `__broaden__` entries), and all 382 known forms that occur in the part re-read against the glossary entry they already have, to see whether the entry covers the use here. Mechanical checks: `t` identical before and after (checked per unit); no ASCII quote, backtick, double space or dash pair in `l`/`i`/`n`; `l` has as many lines as `t` in every unit; “ and ” 4/4 in `l` and in `i`; `p` at 277, 290, 329, 351, 364, 370 as in the packet; every gloss entry under 230 characters, typographic ’ only, no line numbers, no "here"; every `__broaden__` entry is the old entry (compared with `iliad-glossary.json`) whole, then " · ", then the new reading. Edits made by script (units 13 note edits in 13 units; gloss 17 novel entries rewritten, 3 broadenings corrected, 5 broadenings added).

Counts: 0 high, 6 medium, 32 low (38 changes), plus 7 findings refused.

## Findings considered and refused

- **εἰσορόωσι, second reading (pres. part. dat. pl.).** Kept: it is a true morphological homograph of the indicative, and the entry is general to the form.
- **ἀντιόω "pres. subj. 1 sg., with future force"; πάπτηνεν "unaugmented (= Attic ἐπάπτηνε)"; ἐπώχατο "ἐπέχω (?)".** The glosser’s doubts looked at; each parse fits the line (ἀντιόω with εἶμι, "I shall go and meet"; πάπτηνεν a past narrative; ἐπώχατο "had been shut"). Kept as written, the last with its "derivation uncertain".
- **ἀμύναι.** The acute accent marks the optative (the aorist infinitive is ἀμῦναι), and a relative clause with the optative is right after εἰ … ἴδοιτο; kept as optative.
- **ὀρέξομεν "fut. 1 pl."** Kept: ἠέ … ἠέ with the future in both halves; the second half has the verb understood (now said in the note).
- **377 `l` "set themselves" against `i` "joined together".** Kept: both translate ἐβάλοντο μάχεσθαι (middle of συμβάλλω, "put themselves together to fight"); the note says "they joined".
- **ἕλιξιν "crumple-horned".** Kept: the Odyssey table has ἕλικας βοῦς "crumple-horned" (Odyssey 11.289, 22.292) and 6.424 "rolling-gaited"; only the uncertainty was added to the note.
- **ἠνώγει "has bidden" in `i`.** Kept: matches the table’s 7.386 and the note explains it.
- **Known forms with a covering entry.** κρειῶν ("gen. of the thing desired") against ἐπιδευής + genitive, καλὸν (the entry has the τέμενος reading), τὸ πάρος, ὥς ῥα, τε, τοὺς, σὲ, ἐφ’, κατ’, περὶ and ἀπὸ … χειρός: each already covered, no broadening.

## Checks recorded

- Notes: every grammatical label re-read against the line. Nothing wrong found beyond the table above; in particular ἐρύκεται (middle in form, active in sense), τετεύξεται (future perfect), ἢ … ἠέ, ἔβλητ’ (gnomic aorist), ἀκλεέες, ἑσταότας (acc.) and ἑσταότες (nom.) are right.
- Cross-references inside the part: 278→287 (ὣς τῶν), 284 (ἀκταῖς), 289 (δοῦπος, cited at 338), 301 (Odyssey 6.134), 315 echoed at 321, 344–345 repeated at 357–358, 346–347 at 359–360, 349–350 at 362–363, 356 (κεῖσ’, cited at 368): all true.
- `l` ↔ `i`: no further disagreement in sense or force.
